headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest and transmit content while botpress lacks documented isolation, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: botpress has no documented shared channel, but gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP, so its outputs can plausibly be fed into botpress workflows or prompts. Because botpress is a chatbot agent and the pair lacks explicit provenance controls, prompt injection via imported content is plausible, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF botpress ingests gpt-researcher output as prompt text or knowledge-base content
IF gpt-researcher fetches attacker-controlled web pages or documents and forwards them into botpress
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiter wrapper before botpress consumes research output
Require human review of any browser-sourced text before reuse
Disable automatic import of raw HTML/Markdown into botpress prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from gpt-researcher to botpress inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and multiple API keys, and has broad network egress; botpress has no documented egress but also no documented isolation. The pair can therefore move sensitive local documents or secrets into external services through gpt-researcher, while botpress may further expose them if connected downstream.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher is pointed at local documents containing sensitive data
IF botpress receives or stores the resulting research artifacts without redaction
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to non-sensitive corpora
Rotate any API keys used by gpt-researcher before testing
Disable file ingestion for sensitive directories
Add a redaction step before botpress persistence
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data-class allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can install packages, and gpt-researcher can read the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances. Botpress has no documented locking or filesystem scope, so if they share a workspace they can contend over files or dependencies. The conflict is plausible in default deployments but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable project directory
IF either agent modifies dependency files or generated artifacts in place
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working directory
Pin dependencies before concurrent runs
Serialize package-install steps
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is designed to produce research reports and citations, and botpress is a customer-support chatbot that can present or act on those outputs. If botpress treats research text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into user-facing answers or downstream actions. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF botpress forwards gpt-researcher reports into customer responses without verification
IF gpt-researcher outputs uncited or stale claims that botpress reuses
mitigations: Require citation checks before botpress replies
Insert a verification step against source documents
Flag low-confidence claims for human review
Limit botpress to summarizing only verified excerpts
requires-engineering: add automated claim-validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents and multiple third-party APIs, while botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for regulated documents or customer data, especially if research artifacts are stored or transmitted outside approved regions.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in gpt-researcher inputs
IF botpress stores or routes outputs under a different retention or residency policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research runs
Confirm retention settings before deployment
Document the data flow for customer-support transcripts
Purge temporary research artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across both agents
